data.name: Orcs Must Die! 2
data.detailed_description:
You’ve tossed, burned and sliced them by the thousands – now orcs must die more than ever before! Grab a friend and slay orcs in untold numbers in this sequel to the 2011 AIAS Strategy Game of the Year from Robot Entertainment.

Leap back into the fray as a powerful War Mage or crafty Sorceress. Defend new fortresses and dwarven mines, laying waste to thousands of orcs and other monsters with a dizzying array of weapons, spells, guardians, traps, and trinkets. Play co-op with a friend and continue the battle in a brand new campaign mode, or fight to stay alive in the challenging new Endless Mode!

Unlock new defenses and old favorites, upgrade them like never before, and unleash them on the nearest pile of slobbering orcs!

Key Features:

  • Co-Op! - Play as the War Mage, the headstrong hero who charges into danger, or play as the more strategic Sorceress who keeps the mob at bay with mind-control and magic.
  • Story-based Campaign – Pick up where the original game left off with a brand new story-based campaign that you can play in Single-Player or Co-Op!
  • New Endless Mode - Play alone or join a friend to put your skills to the test against endless waves of increasingly difficult enemies.
  • Classic Mode - Steam players who own the original Orcs Must Die! will automatically unlock co-op versions of 10 levels from the original game featuring new enemies!
  • Over 20 Deadly Enemies - Face an army of vile new creatures like Earth Elementals, Trolls, and Bile Bats. And they’ve brought all of your favorite trap-fodder from the original Orcs Must Die! along with them!
  • More than 50 Traps, Weapons, and Guardians – Choose from an enormous armory of new and classic defenses, including an all new assortment of magical trinkets.
  • Massive Upgrade System – With more than 225 persistent trap and weapon upgrades to unlock, you can build an arsenal perfectly suited to your slaying style.
  • Extensive Replayability – Multiple game modes, “Nightmare” difficulty, and an enormous skull-ranking system provide hours of replayability
  • Scoring System and Leaderboard – Compete with your friends for supremacy on single-player and co-op leaderboards!

reviews.review:
My total playtime to 100% w/ DLC: 32.7 hours.

Orcs Must Die 2 is a fun 3D tower defense, but in the sequel, the game was given a co-op option. I enjoyed OMD1 a lot, and I still enjoyed this one, but I don't recommend it. The biggest reason why will be at the bottom (it is crashes. A lot of them).

First, what the game does well:
• There are more traps, weapons, and new trinkets available, creating a wider pool of diversity. 
• The new trinkets are fun, they give passive effects when carried and active effects when activated.
• It has an endless mode, which can feel a bit boring as enemy health drastically scales up. But it does exist.
• Co-op and balancing trap types with your partner can be enjoyable.
• It's still fun!

What it does okay:
• You have to buy new traps, weapons, trinkets, and skins with in-game skulls you earn from playing the game. More on skulls below. While upgrading can be fun, traps feel underpowered until they get upgraded. You go from feeling weak, to feeling very strong later on. I consider this to be a pretty neutral point, although feeling weak early makes the player feel like their traps aren't as valuable.

Let me get into the negative aspects of the game I encountered:
• To unlock everything, you'd have to play far more than the typical two campaign playthroughs you'd normally play. There is a best method for grinding skulls, and it is relatively boring. It feels like skull grinding should have been faster, but this game could have been played very reptitiously in the past. It doesn't necessarily hold up to being a "main game" anymore, so I don't hold it entirely against it.
• More on the above point, if you don't have something upgraded, and you do have other things upgraded, it is often not worth it to use those non-upgraded things at all until they are completed.
• Headshot angles are a bit wonky. I consider myself to have pretty good aim, but either due to where the projectile is sourced, or the hitboxes of certain enemies, it is really only possible to reliably headshot bigger enemies.
• The maps are balanced around co-op. There's a lot of running in some of them if you were to play them solo. Likely too much. And multiple rifts, on often oppositional sides of the map.
• A bit too many of the traps & such are tied to DLC.
• There's less base game campaign levels than in the original game.
• There are two characters you can play, you can choose between the man (war mage) or woman (sorceress). The problem here, is that they have unique trap types, meaning you can't ever access some of them on the other character. The profiles are also different. This feels very bad.
• The game feels a bit too sexualizing of women, in both dialogue and over half the skins for women. The dev was probably a bit too horny cooking this one up. I don't even have anything against these types of games, but this one doesn't really feel like that type of game, you know?

And my Co-op gripes:
• You effectively lose item slots. You get 10 slots to hold your traps, weapons, and trinkets in solo, and 6 each in co-op. This should theoretically work out to a gain of 2, but considering both players will likely select weapon(s) and trinket(s) as well, the amount of trap slots effectively decreases. I wouldn't consider this to be bad per se, but it does make it feel less fun!
• You effectively gain more upgrades playing in co-op if your partner upgrades other towers and weapons, making you weaker if you play solo.

And my biggest complaints, crashes (I was on Windows 10 playing this):
If you crash, you will probably crash with repetition. Far too often. I had to restart my computer many times before playing this game, because sometimes it wouldn't even load past the starting screen. Sometimes I'd crash at the end of levels (co-op OR in singleplayer). Restarting delayed it, but it inevitably I'd end up crashing again. This is very bad news for Endless mode especially. To make it all worse, if you crash, not only does your leaderboard rank not get saved (not a concern for me), your career kills would not get saved. The achievement for killing 50,000 orcs was essentially my last achievement, even though I should've had it done quite a ways before some of the others. I estimate I lost probably 12,000 kills at least to crashes. For reference, I did wave 50 endless and wave 40 endless solo, and my co-operative partner (who never crashed, and only played with me) at the end of our 2 campaign runs had 7,000 more kills than me. On the plus side, you still get the skulls at the end of the level and the map is flagged as completed properly, even if you crash at the end. 

I get this game is old. But with the amount of crashing I experience, I can not recommend it. It will likely be a gamble. My co-op partner never crashed, but I still crashed in singleplayer, so I can't even say it was co-op related at all. Despite the game's age, I can find threads about crash issues dating back 10+ years ago. For this reason alone, even though I had fun with this game, I would not recommend it.
